newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas sinks late, ends near day's lows.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas sinks late, ends near day's lows.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended near the day's lows Tuesday in a sluggish session, with August briefly driven below support by a late wave of technical selling and long liquidation, market sources said.
August slipped 2.9 cents to close on support at $2.11 per million British thermal units after briefly dipping to $2.105. Sept settled 2.3 cents lower at $2.113. Others also ended down.

"Technically, we went out on the lows and could see more pressure, but fundamentally, it feels supported. I think anything below $2.00 (basis August) is out of the question," said one East Coast trader, noting cash held today.

While mixed weather forecasts and typically soft early July demand may encourage the bears, traders said steady injections and continued heat in Texas and the West should be enough to limit any slide near-term.
Temperatures in the Midwest and Northeast should fluctuate around normal over the next six to 10 days, while parts of the Southeast may be above-normal during the period.

Chart traders agreed August's dip Tuesday below trendline support could lead to a test of the recent low at $2.08, with a move to next support in the $2.05 area possible. Resistance remained first at $2.15 and then along the trendline at $2.27. Further selling was likely at the recent $2.36 high and then at the $2.415 contract high.
Early injection estimates for Wednesday's weekly AGA stock report range from 75-105 bcf versus a 93 bcf build last year.

In the cash Tuesday, Gulf Coast prices were unchanged to a penny lower in the low-teens. Midcon pipes were steady to up slightly at about $2.03-2.05. New York city gate gas was quoted modestly lower in the low-to-mid $2.40s.
The NYMEX Henry Hub 12-month strip fell two cents to $2.191. NYMEX said 17,579 contracts traded, up from Monday's revised tally of 12,465.
NYMEX natgas trade will close at 1300 EDT Thursday ahead of the Independence Day holiday Friday.

On the KCBT, August finished 3.8 cents lower at $1.982, while deferreds ended down by 2.5 to 4.1 cents. The East/West spread widened by 0.9 cent to 12.8 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 167 lots traded, up from Monday's total of 134.
